meta.stress_definition: Departures ≥15 min late or cancelled / all scheduled departures in next 2h
meta.model_note: Replay uses the predeclared tabular model. Nov–Dec chronological holdout · overlapping 2h targets · per-model inference time (graph includes base prediction). Lowest test error is descriptive; full calibration, intervals and rolling folds are linked.
meta.scenario_limitation: Held-out baseline MAE 920 minutes vs actual mean 1699 per airport/4h interval (61 days). This coarse aggregate fit limits scenario interpretation. Resource effects are hypothetical; passenger, crew, maintenance and capacity feasibility are absent. Reductions are simulated, not causal savings.
limitations: Final BTS schedules proxy advance schedules; no historical schedule revisions.
Actual departures and NOAA weather assumed available one hour after occurrence. BTS itself is retrospective.
Four hubs and four reporting carriers; regional affiliates and much of the network are excluded.
Day examples selected after observing holdout outcomes to cover ordinary and severe conditions; models were not tuned on them.
Overlapping windows cannot be added into daily savings. Cancellation delay duration is omitted from simulated minutes.
Retrospective tail chains are diagnostic; forecasts and allocation never use future actual aircraft assignments.
Nominal 90% tabular prediction intervals cover 81.5% of final-holdout outcomes; temporal undercoverage limits uncertainty claims.

findings.question: Which observations disappear from delay averages?
findings.finding: 24,539 arrival delays are missing (1.52%); 20,229 flights are cancelled. 881,126 departures have negative delay.
findings.limitation: Missingness categories overlap. Delay observations exclude many cancelled/diverted flights, and this selected subnetwork is not the US system.
findings.implication: Show cancellation rates alongside signed observed delays; never replace missing arrival delay with zero.

findings.question: How much does disruption change by month?
findings.denominator: 841,926 selected-carrier departures from four hubs, grouped by reporting month.
findings.finding: Month 7 has 38.5% disrupted departures versus 14.8% in month 10.
findings.limitation: One reporting year and changing carrier/airport schedules cannot establish a stable long-run seasonal pattern.
findings.implication: Evaluate against seasonal baselines and chronological holdouts; avoid random train/test splits.

findings.question: How much do airport/carrier cohorts differ?
findings.denominator: 841,926 hub-origin scheduled departures; cells include their actual cohort schedules.
findings.finding: DFW/AA has 35.3% disruption (n=166,286), versus 18.1% for DEN/DL (n=12,439).
findings.limitation: These unadjusted groups differ in routes, schedule times and exposure. They do not establish carrier quality or causal airport effects.
findings.implication: Compare within cohorts and include airport identity and schedule workload in the forecast; preserve the scope denominator.

findings.question: Do late inbound aircraft coincide with late following departures?
findings.denominator: 724,524 validated adjacent observed-tail hub-turn links with reported preceding arrival and following departure delays.
findings.finding: previous arrival <15 min late: 12.7% following departures late (n=590,930); previous arrival >=15 min late: 56.8% following departures late (n=133,594).
findings.limitation: Retrospective same-tail continuity omits flights at nonhub turns, overnight turns, missing tails, crews and passenger connections. Association is not a causal effect.
findings.implication: Use validated chains for retrospective diagnosis; deployable forecasts must use only cutoff-available network state, not future aircraft assignments.

findings.question: Does recent visibility separate disruption risk?
findings.denominator: 28,471 airport cutoffs with accepted visibility, weather age ≤3h, and a complete target; overlapping two-hour exposures.
findings.finding: visibility <5 km: 35.9% disruption (n=1,056 cutoffs); visibility >=5 km: 24.5% disruption (n=27,415 cutoffs).
findings.limitation: Unadjusted association confounds seasonality, hubs and storms. Hourly two-hour windows overlap; NOAA publication time is assumed observation time plus one hour.
findings.implication: Use recent weather as a candidate feature and verify added value on chronological holdouts before making operational claims.
